Article Title: Times Prime rolls out Rs 1 lakh reward envelopes across 5,000 Daalchini vending machines
Article Text:
Times Prime takes 'Born to Reward' to Daalchini vending machines

Times Prime has partnered with Daalchini as part of its ‘Born to Reward’ birthday campaign, placing 1,00,000 limited-edition reward envelopes across 5,000 Daalchini vending machines in Mumbai and Delhi.The campaign, which runs from September 23 to October 31, offers consumers reward envelopes priced at Rs 10, each containing a voucher with benefits worth over Rs 5,000 from participating Times Prime partners.Five of the envelopes contain Golden Tickets, with each ticket offering a reward package worth up to Rs 20,000. The package includes enhanced benefits from participating Times Prime partners as well as access to an exclusive Times Prime event.Consumers can locate participating Daalchini vending machines through timesoffer.daalchini.co.in.The vending machine activation is part of Times Prime’s broader birthday campaign, which began on its app. From September 23 to 30, members unlocked a new partner offer each day, with the offers remaining available for redemption for the rest of the campaign.The offers cover categories including travel, shopping, wellness, beauty, healthcare and lifestyle, with participating brands including Flipkart Flights, Klook, IGP, MeraDoc, FirstCry, Geetanjali Salon, GIVA and Duolingo.Prerna Kalra, co-founder and CEO of Daalchini, said the partnership reflects the growing role of vending machines in providing consumers with instant access to products and offers.“India’s instant commerce story has been about delivery in minutes. We believe the next chapter is zero-wait, with value available the moment you walk past a machine. Gift cards and vouchers are a big step in that direction, and Times Prime’s birthday is the perfect moment to put rewards into consumers’ hands, literally,” Kalra said.Times Prime is a digital lifestyle membership platform from Times Internet that offers subscriptions, benefits and experiences across entertainment, dining, travel, shopping, wellness and other lifestyle categories.
Article Summary: Times Prime has partnered with Daalchini as part of its ‘Born to Reward’ birthday campaign. The campaign, which runs from September 23 to October 31, offers consumers reward envelopes priced at Rs 10. Each containing a voucher with benefits worth over Rs 5,000 from participating Times Prime partners.

NEW DELHI: A petition has been filed in the Supreme Court challenging the appointments of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi.Through the petition, the petitioner has sought a writ of quo warranto against Kumar, Sandhu and Joshi and challenged the validity of their appointments to the Election Commission , according to Live Law report.The plea contends that their appointments did not follow the procedure prescribed under the CEC and other ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.The petitioner has argued that under Section 6 of the Act, a panel of five names should have been prepared for each vacancy before the appointments were made. Article Title: Beyond condoms: WHO blueprint for new male contraceptives
Article Text:
Contraceptive choices for men. (Reuters)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Men could have more contraceptive choices beyond condoms and vasectomy, with the World Health Organization (WHO) releasing its first global blueprint for developing novel male contraceptives, including daily pills or gels, longer-acting injections and implants, sperm-function blockers and reversible methods that block sperm transport.The WHO's Target Product Profiles (TPPs) do not approve or launch any new contraceptive. Instead, they set minimum and optimal standards for the effectiveness, safety, reversibility, acceptability and affordability of future male contraceptives. The framework covers three approaches: suppressing sperm production, inhibiting sperm function and blocking sperm transmission or transport.The move comes as research into male contraception gathers pace, with several candidates already in clinical trials. RISUG (reversible inhibition of sperm under guidance), developed in India, has completed Phase 1 and Phase 2 studies, while another hydrogel-based method, ADAM, is in Phase 1 trials.Hormonal candidates including nestorone/testosterone gel, dimethandrolone undecanoate (DMAU) and 11β-methyl-19-nortestosterone dodecylcarbonate (11β-MNTDC) are also being investigated.For methods that suppress sperm production, WHO's minimum target is for 90% of men to achieve sperm concentrations of 1 million or fewer sperm per millilitre within 12 weeks, with a 12-month cumulative pregnancy rate of no more than 7%.The optimal target is 95% achieving this level within eight weeks, with the pregnancy rate at 3% or less.The proposed methods include daily tablets or gels, injections every three, six or 12 months and implants lasting at least a year. WHO's optimal profile also calls for sperm concentrations to return to the normal reference range within six months of stopping treatment.Another strategy is to leave sperm present but disable functions needed for fertilisation, such as motility and capacitation. A third is to block sperm transport through the vas deferens, potentially using reversible hydrogels, or temporarily block ejaculation with medication.WHO said the field is rapidly progressing, with several candidates in advanced clinical trials. The new profiles are intended to provide developers and regulators with a common framework for bringing future male contraceptives through research and development.
Article Summary: The WHO's Target Product Profiles do not approve or launch any new contraceptive. Instead, they set minimum and optimal standards for the effectiveness, safety, reversibility, acceptability and affordability of future male contraceptives. The framework covers three approaches: suppressing sperm production, inhibiting sperm function and blocking sperm transmission or transport.

Article Title: WHO puts stroke, cancer, mental health on 10-year traditional medicine research agenda
Article Text:
The World Health Organization has set forth a comprehensive research agenda for the upcoming decade, focusing on pivotal health conditions such as stroke, mental health, cancer, and reproductive health.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: From stroke and cancer to mental health and pain management, the World Health Organization has identified major health conditions for research into traditional, complementary and integrative medicine over the next decade.Its 2025-2034 research agenda identifies stroke, mental health, pain management, musculoskeletal conditions, cancer, metabolic and endocrine disorders, and reproductive health and childbirth as priority areas. Prevention and health promotion, healthy ageing and healthy childhood are also included.The report highlights a striking mismatch between disease burden and research. Stroke ranks third globally in causes of mortality and disability, yet less than 1% of traditional, complementary and integrative medicine-funded grants address the condition. Mental health ranks eighth among contributors to disability-adjusted life years, but the review found very few or no grants specifically focused on mental health conditions. Musculoskeletal conditions are also a prominent cause of disability globally but remain under-researched relative to their burden.Cancer, too, features among the priority areas, with the report noting rising global incidence and calling for research into integrative oncology and palliative care.For metabolic health and endocrine disorders, WHO identifies the need for stronger evidence, including longer-term studies on conditions such as type 2 diabetes and metabolic syndrome.WHO says the aim is to generate stronger evidence on effectiveness, safety, regulation and health-system integration so countries can make informed decisions about the role of these approaches in healthcareThe research agenda also puts patient safety under the spotlight. It calls for studies on herb-drug interactions, monitoring and reporting of adverse events, regulatory and quality-assurance systems, and the safe integration of traditional, complementary and integrative medicine into primary healthcare.The push comes against a broader funding gap. WHO says traditional, complementary and integrative medicine is widely used globally, with use reaching up to 80% of populations in some settings, while less than 1% of global health research funding is directed towards research in the field.India has a direct connection to the agenda. The WHO report acknowledges financial support from the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India, for its development and publication. India was also among the health ministries that participated in the Second WHO Global Summit on Traditional Medicine, held in New Delhi in December 2025.The report, however, is a research-prioritisation framework rather than a clinical guideline or recommendation to use any particular traditional medicine.
Article Summary: The 2025-2034 research agenda identifies stroke, mental health, pain management, musculoskeletal conditions, cancer, metabolic and endocrine disorders. Prevention and health promotion, healthy ageing and healthy childhood are also included. Stroke ranks third globally in causes of mortality and disability, yet less than 1% of traditional, complementary and integrative medicine-funded grants address the condition.

Article Title: Stock market crash today: BSE Sensex tanks over 1,000 points; Nifty50 at 22,231 - top reasons for fall
Article Text:
Adding to the pressure on markets, Brent crude prices rose another 2%.

Why is stock market down today?

RBI’s policy stance change

US bond yields

soar to 24-year high

Oil jumps above $102/barrel

FIIs continue to sell

Fed rate hike worries

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)

Stock market crash today: BSE Sensex and Nifty50 , the Indian equity benchmarks, crashed in trade on Thursday, with both indices down over 1%. Investors reacted to the RBI’s policy tightening and repo rate hike, continued FII selling and other negative factors. BSE Sensex plunged over 1,000 points while NSE Nifty50 slipped to 22,231 levels.At closing, Nifty50 was at 22,231.80, down 371.25 points or 1.64%. BSE Sensex was at 71,593.24, down 1,045.46 points or 1.44%. The sharp decline erased over Rs 11 lakh crore from the combined market capitalisation of companies listed on the BSE.ITC, Adani Ports, IndiGo, Power Grid and Reliance Industries (RIL) were among the biggest losers on the Sensex, with their shares declining as much as 4%. On the other hand, Titan and major IT stocks such as Tech Mahindra, HCL Technologies, TCS and Infosys gained up to 2%, providing some support to the benchmark index.The RBI delivered its first rate increase in nearly four years. However, market analysts viewed the central bank’s decision to move its policy stance from ‘neutral’ to ‘calibrated tightening’, against a difficult global geopolitical backdrop, as the more significant signal for markets.Jefferies expects the RBI to raise interest rates by around 100 basis points during the current tightening cycle.Nomura also pointed to the change in stance as an unexpected development. “We believe this was aimed at anchoring inflation expectations and building a buffer against adverse global conditions. However, the message was mixed, with the MPC clarifying that “calibrated tightening” only signalled “no rate cuts”, and indicated data dependence going forward,” it added.VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist, Geojit Investments Limited says that the calibrated tightening stance of the RBI has implications for markets.“With two more rate hikes of 25bp each likely in this rate hiking cycle, there will be pressure on valuations rising from higher fixed income returns. Investor preferences also might shift marginally towards interest inelastic segments like pharmaceuticals,” he says.The global selloff in bonds intensified, sending yields to their highest levels in several years. The US 30-year bond yield climbed above 5.71%, while the yield on benchmark 10-year notes rose past 5.3%. The two-year note yield also moved close to 4.9%.Rising bond yields generally make debt markets more appealing to investors, which can increase pressure on emerging-market equities. Since bond prices and yields move in opposite directions, a sharp rise in yields indicates significant selling in the bond market.Adding to the pressure on markets, Brent crude prices rose another 2% to move above $102 per barrel. Investors remained worried about the security of Middle East oil supplies as attacks on shipments increased in the Gulf and around the strategically important Strait of Hormuz.Tankers travelling through the Strait of Hormuz faced the highest number of attacks in a single week since the Iran war began earlier this year, even as Gulf producers raised exports. The increase in attacks came as crude shipments from the Gulf increased, but with greater risks and higher costs for cargoes and crews. On Wednesday, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said a tanker north of Qatar had been hit by multiple projectiles, resulting in casualties.Meanwhile, US crude inventories fell by 3.2 million barrels last week to 424.1 million barrels, according to the Energy Information Administration on Wednesday. A Reuters poll of analysts had forecast a smaller decline of 1.7 million barrels.The record selling spree of FIIs continues, exacerbated by the rising bond yields. Foreign investors continued their selling spree in Indian equities on Wednesday, offloading shares worth more than Rs 6,121 crore on a net basis, according to provisional NSE data. Their net selling has now reached nearly Rs 57,000 crore across nine straight sessions through Wednesday.Since the start of September, FIIs have been net sellers in 20 of the 25 trading sessions. Their sustained selling, despite brief periods of buying, has continued to weigh on Dalal Street since the Middle East war began earlier this year.VK Vijayakumar notes that a distinct and strong trend in the market in recent months has been the increasing preference for growth stocks over value stocks.“Growth stocks are being accumulated at high valuations while value stocks are languishing at fair valuations. Sustained selling in large-caps by the FIIs have contributed significantly to this trend. With the US 10-year bond yield hovering above 5.3%, FIIs will continue to sell on every rally. This will put the Nifty large-caps under pressure for some more time,” he warns.“A reversal in this trend will happen only when FIIs turn buyers, and there is no clarity on when this will happen. In brief, this frustrating period in the market might continue for some more time. Remaining invested in value stocks will be rewarded in the long run. Investors should also look at the good opportunities in fixed income in this rising rate environment,” he adds.Minutes from the Federal Reserve's meeting showed a split among policymakers last month over the case for raising interest rates. Some officials believed a hike was needed to contain the effects of energy and other price shocks, while a more hawkish group saw higher rates as necessary to guard against emerging inflation driven by demand.Traders currently see only an 18% probability of a rate increase later this month, while the odds of a December hike are being priced at 80%, according to CME's FedWatch tool, as cited by Reuters.
Article Summary: BSE Sensex plunged over 1,000 points while NSE Nifty50 slipped to 22,231 levels. Investors reacted to the RBI’s policy tightening and repo rate hike, continued FII selling and other negative factors. The sharp decline erased over Rs 11 lakh crore from the combined market capitalisation of companies listed on the BSE.

Article Title: NTPC identifies 3 locations for nuclear power projects
Article Text:
The public sector powerhouse, NTPC, has earmarked three strategic locations across India for the establishment of nuclear power plants.

NEW DELHI: Public sector NTPC has identified three locations, one each in Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Odisha, to set up nuclear power plants as it aims to add 30GW of nuclear capacity across 14 states by 2047.The company has submitted detailed feasibility reports for each site to the Atomic Energy Commission for approval. NTPC is also exploring technology collaborations with global players such as Holtec International and Westinghouse of the US, Rosatom of Russia and EDF of France for pressurised water reactor projects to be deployed at these locations, said an official aware of the development.With an installed power generation capacity of 89GW, including thermal, hydro and renewable capacity, the company is targeting 149GW by 2032 and 244GW by 2037, besides adding significant battery and pumped storage capacity. It has set up NTPC Parmanu Urja Nigam Ltd as its wholly owned nuclear subsidiary to foray into nuclear power. Its first nuclear project in Rajasthan’s Mahi Banswara, comprising four 700-MW units, however, is being developed through Anushakti Vidhyut Nigam Ltd, a joint venture with Nuclear Power Corporation of India.The three identified locations, if approved, will have 2-4GW of nuclear capacity each, the official said.NTPC entered into non-disclosure agreements with Rosatom and EDF earlier this year to explore technology collaboration for deploying large pressurised water reactor projects in India.“Technology transfer and localisation will be key factors in finalising the technology. There will be a separate joint venture with a global player for technology and design engineering,” said the official.Fuel availability will also be an important consideration in finalising the technology, the official said, adding that fuel sourcing falls within the domain of the Centre.
Article Summary: NTPC has identified three locations, one each in Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Odisha, to set up nuclear power plants. The company has submitted detailed feasibility reports for each site to the Atomic Energy Commission for approval. NTPC is also exploring technology collaborations with global players such as Holtec International and Westinghouse.

Article Title: Rupee may be undervalued, markets can be irrational: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra
Article Text:
File photo: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra

Sensex snaps winning run

MUMBAI: Reserve Bank of India governor Sanjay Malhotra said the rupee was undervalued and the central bank would intervene to ensure orderly movement in the currency market even as it closed at 96.78 on Wednesday, down 36 paise from its previous close, after falling to a five-month low of 96.85 during the day."By a number of estimates, including the real effective exchange rate, the rupee is not overvalued. It may be undervalued," Malhotra said at a press conference after the MPC meeting. He was responding to a question on whether the rupee market was irrational."Markets can be quite irrational in the short run. It's only in the long run that they are able to find the right value," he said.The governor said RBI would support the rupee's orderly movement and help it find its "correct value", while ensuring there was no excessive volatility.Malhotra also said a correction in the valuation of global AI stocks could redirect foreign capital to emerging markets such as India. He said a correction in AI stocks would not have a major negative impact on India and "if at all, there may be" a positive impact.Malhotra said that US tariffs and the absence of a trade deal would be a negative but could be offset by a trade deal with other countries.Despite a robust services trade surplus and strong net remittance receipts, the current account deficit widened in July because of a higher merchandise trade deficit, Malhotra said.The merchandise trade deficit rose to $58.7 billion in July and Aug from $55.1 billion in the same period a year earlier, mainly because of higher imports of electronic goods and crude oil. On external financing, Malhotra said net FDI had shown sustained improvement, with inflows rising to $13.8 billion in the first four months of the year from $9.6 billion in the corresponding period a year earlier. The increase was driven by higher gross inflows and a slowdown in the growth of outward FDI."Robust gross FDI reflects the strong interest of global investors in India," he said. FPI recorded net outflows of $10.3 billion during the period up to Oct 5. However, capital-flow measures announced in the June policy had supported inflows, he said. The balance of payments is consequently expected to record a healthy surplus this year.Malhotra also clarified that the new trade rules are aimed at improving ease of business and do not impose a reporting burden on individuals who get paid from overseas for software or other services. Nor does it apply to individuals paying for software or some subscriptions. Small exporters can use a self-declaration for bills up to Rs 10 lakh; and banks, not exporters or importers, handle reporting on the RBI's system. The aim is to simplify trade procedures while improving RBI's data on services exports, he said.After a two-session gain, sensex slid on Wednesday after RBI hiked interest rates for the first time in over three-and-a-half years. Sensex closed 429 points down at 72,639 points while on NSE, Nifty closed 173 points down at 22,603 points.On BSE, two indices-PSU banks and housing finance-each closed nearly 1% up while two other indices-bankex and financial services-closed barely changed.
Article Summary: After a two-session gain, sensex slid on Wednesday after RBI hiked interest rates for the first time in over three-and-a-half years. Sensex closed 429 points down at 72,639 points while on NSE, Nifty closed 173 points down. On external financing, Malhotra said net FDI had shown sustained improvement.

Article Title: Stark 73% decline in the average size of monitored wildlife populations since 1970, India presents ground for hope: WWF Living Planet Report
Article Text:
Representative image

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: There was a stark 73% decline in the “average size of monitored wildlife populations” globally over a 52-year period (1970-2022), whereas India became one of the most important countries that were successfully involved in wildlife recovery by turning around the populations of certain animals, including tigers, one-horned rhino and Ganga river dolphins, according to WWF’s biennial Living Planet Report (LPR) released on Thursday.Though the LPR remains silent on country-specific data, experts explaining certain points ahead of the release noted “significant changes” in biodiversity in India where nine species of mammals figured in the “critically endangered” list, 39% of 942 bird species reported “clear decline” and 32% (136 species) of the amphibians have been “threatened” by a combination of factors including agricultural practices and climate change.Nine mammals classified as critically endangered (CR) in India under International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) criteria are Kashmir Stag/Hangul, Malabar Large-spotted Civet, Chinese Pangolin, Andaman Shrew, Jenkin’s Shrew, Nicobar Shrew, Namdapha Flying Squirrel, Large Rock Rat and Leafletted Leaf-nosed Bat.The report is based on Living Planet Index (LPI), which tracks how species populations are faring around the world.The Index, produced by Zoological Society of London, includes 35,803 population trends of 5,790 vertebrate species (mammals, birds, amphibians, reptiles and fish) from 1970 to 2022.It noted the strongest decline in freshwater ecosystems (-85%), followed by terrestrial (-69%) and then marine (-59%) over the 1970 baseline. Region-wise, Latin America and the Caribbean registered the highest decline of 95%, followed by Africa (80%), Asia-Pacific (49%), North America (28%), and Europe and Central Asia (23%).The report said the “habitat loss and degradation” are the most frequently reported threat affecting monitored wildlife populations, followed by overexploitation, climate change, pollution, invasive species and disease. “These threats are, in turn, driven by broader systemic failures across the food, energy and finance systems,” it said.Although the overall trend is negative due to the magnitude of the declining trends, LPR noted that half of the populations included in the Index are “stable or increasing”. It highlighted recoveries in populations of green turtles, bluefin tuna, tigers and southern African elephants, which demonstrate that targeted conservation interventions can deliver proven results.Asked about the biggest takeaway in the LPR that flagged an upward trend in the numbers of species in India including tigers, Asiatic lion, common leopard and snow leopard, Sejal Worah, programme director, WWF-India, said one big message is that the country can actually turn around wildlife populations and species with the right combination of factors, including political will, required finances, civil society engagement and involvement with local communities. India has shown that wildlife recovery is possible, she added.WWF-India, during its pre-release presentation, however, underlined certain significant changes in biodiversity in India. It noted that the country is home to around 135 bat species that face neglect due to a “lack of research” and are threatened by urbanisation, deforestation, land-use changes and climate change. It also said that freshwater fish are among the most threatened vertebrates.“The LPR 2026 is both a stark reminder of the scale of the biodiversity crisis and a message of hope. While the LPI continues to highlight significant declines in monitored wildlife populations, the report also shows that these declines are not inevitable. Species recoveries, including those of tigers in India and globally, demonstrate what sustained conservation action, collaboration and long-term commitment can achieve,” said Ravi Singh, secretary general & CEO, WWF-India.Referring to data, the report said, “Although the overall global trend is negative, half (50%) of the populations included in the LPI are stable (7%) or increasing (43%). The magnitude of the declining trends, however, exceeds that of the increasing trends resulting in an average decline of 73% for the global LPI.”It, however, clarified that the percentage change in the index reflects the cumulative average proportional change in monitored animal population sizes at sites around the world since 1970, not the number of individual animals lost, nor the number of populations lost.It also said that the LPI are not directly comparable as they contain different sets of species (967 more populations and 295 more species have been added to the dataset since the LPR 2024) and cover a longer period each time.
Article Summary: There was a stark 73% decline in the “average size of monitored wildlife populations’ globally over a 52-year period (1970-2022) India became one of the most important countries that were successfully involved in wildlife recovery. Latin America and the Caribbean registered the highest decline of 95%, followed by Africa (80%), Asia-Pacific (49%), North America (28%) and Europe and Central Asia (23%)

NEW DELHI: The news of TMC chairperson Mamata Banerjee arriving in Delhi on Thursday evening has heightened the anticipation that an appointment sought by INDIA bloc for a meeting with President Droupadi Murmu over the functioning of Election Commission and the SIR process may be coming soon.Opposition INDIA bloc parties have agreed to restrict their delegation to 10 as sought by the President Secretariat, sources said.There was no confirmation from opposition parties as of Wednesday night if they have received an appointment from the President’s Secretariat. Opposition has sought time any day between Oct 7-9 from the President and are awaiting a confirmation, sources said.The decision to write over this issue to the President was taken at the INDIA bloc meeting on Sept 30. After that, it is learnt that the bloc wrote seeking time from the President. It was conveyed by the President's secretariat that it would need to restrict their contingent of leaders to not more than 10, sources said.The INDIA bloc has now written back agreeing to the request and they have been asked to restrict their delegation to 10 members, sources said.Meanwhile, even as the Opposition awaits eagerly to hear from the President's secretariat for an appointment, CPI(M)'s Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas shared that his petition, seeking urgent constitutional intervention to safeguard the integrity of the Election Commission, the electoral rolls and the democratic franchise, has been forwarded to the legislative department of the govt.Brittas has received a reply from Rashtrapati Bhawan where it has been highlighted that the legislative department has to look into the petition and communicate the action taken in the matter to the petitioner directly.In his petition dated September 23, Brittas also drew the attention of the President to the pending parliamentary notice in Rajya Sabha seeking the removal of the Chief Election Commissioner.He recalled that a fresh notice was submitted in the Rajya Sabha on 24 April 2026, signed by 73 MPs, invoking the constitutional and statutory provisions governing removal for proved misbehaviour and setting out nine grounds in support of the notice.He has urged that the constitutional process contemplated under Article 324(5) be allowed to proceed without obstruction and that the Government extend the cooperation necessary for Parliament to discharge its constitutional responsibility.Brittas also urged that the President ensure that the union govt's position before the Supreme Court supports effective protection of the franchise, including the annulment of the SIR exercise wherever it is found to be without authority of law or contrary to constitutional safeguards.
Article Summary: Opposition parties have agreed to restrict their delegation to 10 as sought by the President Secretariat. Opposition has sought time any day between Oct 7-9 from the President and are awaiting a confirmation. CPI(M)'s Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas shared that his petition, seeking urgent constitutional intervention has been forwarded to the legislative department of the govt.

Article Title: Centre cites Supreme Court order, seeks to void Jharkhand DGP appointment
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Wednesday agreed to hear an application by Centre seeking the annulment of the appointment of Tadasha Mishra as Jharkhand DGP on the ground that it was in violation of procedures laid down in SC's 2006 Prakash Singh judgement.Arguing that the appointments of the last two DGPs were also illegal, Centre said Mishra was appointed the state's police chief just a day before she was to retire, which was in conflict with the SC order that disapproved the practice among states to appoint DGPs on the last date of their tenure so that the person remained in the crucial position for two more years.SC had also clarified that the officers who are empanelled by the state, as far as practicable, must have two years of service left. Solicitor general Tushar Mehta said though an application on the matter was filed more than a month ago, it had not yet been listed for hearing. A bench headed by CJI Surya Kant directed it to be listed for Thursday.Centre questioned the legality of Jharkhand's 'Selection and Appointment of DGP (Head of Police Force) Regulation, 2025 and said the regulations are ex-facie violative of various SC directives, especially its ruling that a state could pick DGP from among those on a panel prepared by UPSC.A petition challenging the validity of the 2025 regulations was transferred from Jharkhand HC to SC in Aug last year. Jharkhand govt appointed Mishra as DGP on Dec 30 last year after amending its own 2025 regulations, which too mandated six months residual service prior to superannuation. MHA had written to Jharkhand to cancel the appointment and take steps to appoint a new DGP.

NEW DELHI: CUET-UG 2027 could see some of its biggest changes yet - fewer subjects, shorter papers and a new grouping system aimed at ensuring that a student can finish the entire entrance test in a single day instead of making repeated trips to examination centres.The ministry of education, University Grants Commission and National Testing Agency are working on a formula to shorten the overall examination cycle and simplify the experience for candidates, sources said.At present, a candidate can take up to five subjects in CUET-UG, with each paper lasting 60 minutes.Under one proposal being examined, the duration of individual papers could be reduced so that even a student taking five subjects can complete all tests within about 180 to 200 minutes.Another option under discussion is whether the maximum number of subjects should be reduced from five to four. Sources said senior officials of the education ministry , UGC and NTA recently discussed the proposed changes and asked officials to examine how the examination could be compressed without affecting university admission requirements.A key part of the plan is to create subject groups based on commonly chosen combinations.This would allow NTA to schedule related papers together and complete a candidate’s examination in one sitting or on the same day.For example, physics, chemistry and biology could form one group for those seeking admission to science programmes. General studies could be added as a fourth paper where universities give weightage to its score. The idea is to bu-ild these groups around eligibility rules followed by universities.For instance, a student seeking admission to physics (Hons) at DU could choose the relevant three-subject combination rather than taking papers not required for the course.Officials believe such grouping could reduce the number of examination days and make scheduling easier. It could also end the problem of students having to travel to examination centres on different days for different papers. The proposals will depend on consultations with universities and the testing agency.
Article Summary: The ministry of education, University Grants Commission and National Testing Agency are working on a formula to shorten the overall examination cycle. A key part of the plan is to create subject groups based on commonly chosen combinations. This would allow NTA to schedule related papers together and complete a candidate’s examination in one sitting or on the same day.

NEW DELHI: Seed industry bodies FSII and NSAI on Wednesday demanded that the government allow commercial cultivation of herbicide-tolerant Bt (HTBt) cotton at the earliest, as the crop variety is being grown illegally in some parts of the country, creating a Rs 1,500 crore informal seed market.The Federation of Seed Industry of India (FSII) and the National Seed Association of India (NSAI) stressed the need to introduce high-yielding varieties and new technologies to boost domestic cotton production and reduce imports.India's cotton production stands at around 29 million bales (of 170 kg each).A study, Unauthorised Cultivation of HTBt Cotton in India: Extent, Drivers and Implications, was conducted by the South Asia Biotechnology Centre (SABC) with the support of these two associations. It covered 16 districts across Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan, combining farmer surveys, supply-chain assessment and ELISA-based gene testing."Unauthorised herbicide-tolerant Bt (HTBt) cotton was grown on 65-72 lakh acres in Kharif 2025-26, or 24-30 per cent of India's total cotton area, sustaining an informal seed market worth an estimated Rs 1,500 crore," FSII Chairman Ajai Rana told reporters.He informed that 1.25 crore packets of HTBt seed are being sold, currently worth Rs 1,500 crore. The total size of the cotton seed market is 5.5 crore packets worth Rs 6,000 crore.Sales of legal Bt cotton seeds have declined."The government should fast-track the approval of HT Bt cotton," he said, adding that Mahyco has already made an application for this purpose in 2024.The association also demanded changes in glyphosate label claims. The product is used for weed management in the cotton crop."Farmers are not breaking the law out of choice. They are paying a black-market premium because the regulatory system has not given them the technology they need," Rana said.The study found that farmers are actively bypassing formal channels and paying a premium technology fee to the black market just to secure operational survival and crop insurance, the FSII said."Unchecked use of unapproved genes and unmonitored glyphosate spraying could breed resistant pests and weeds that devastate cotton productivity," said Dr C D Mayee, President, Indian Society for Cotton Improvement and President, South Asia Biotechnology Centre.The study pointed out that labour shortages are driving the shift. Weed control with glyphosate costs Rs 750-850 an acre, against Rs 12,000-15,000 for manual weeding. Glyphosate use rose 26 per cent in a year, from 27,721 kilolitres in 2024-25 to 35,642 kilolitres in 2025-26."Due to a drop in productivity per acre, India has lost self-sufficiency in cotton production and become an importer of cotton. To regain self-sufficiency and revive the cotton economy, regulatory approval of herbicide-tolerant cotton and the pink bollworm trait should be a national priority," Rana said.
Article Summary: Seed industry bodies FSII and NSAI on Wednesday demanded that the government allow commercial cultivation of herbicide-tolerant Bt cotton. NEW DELHI: Aiming to expedite transmission projects, power ministry has issued fresh guidelines for determining compensation to landowners for laying inter-state transmission lines, fixing separate rates for the Right of Way (RoW) corridor and land used for tower foundations.Nearly 50GW of renewable energy projects are estimated to be delayed due to the lack of inter-state transmission connectivity needed to evacuate clean electricity. Ratings agency ICRA had also pointed out in July that transmission projects faced significant execution challenges related to land acquisition and RoW issues, leading to delays and grid curtailment. It estimated Rs 5-6 lakh crore of capital expenditure in the sector over the next five years.In a report tabled in Parliament last year, the parliamentary standing committee on energy had pointed out that issues related to RoW compensation, land acquisition and delays in environmental clearances were among the major hurdles in laying transmission lines.Officials said the guidelines will apply to transmission lines of 66 kV and above, unless a state govt has already notified its own compensation policy.The guidelines are aimed at bringing uniformity in compensation for landowners affected by transmission projects.As per the guidelines, compensation will be based on the prevailing market value of land determined by a market rate committee headed by the district magistrate or deputy commissioner. This will apply in cases where the market value of land is lower than the prevailing circle rate. The committee will include officials from the revenue department, the sub-divisional magistrate, an administrative representative and representatives of the local civic body.The guidelines also prescribe a mechanism to determine market value where there are disputes. The committee will appoint three valuers selected from a list available through the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India, with valuation carried out along the transmission line alignment. Provisions have also been made for the committee to settle grievances relating to land rates.
Article Summary: The guidelines are aimed at bringing uniformity in compensation for landowners affected by transmission projects. Compensation will be based on the prevailing market value of land determined by a market rate committee. Provisions have also been made for the committee to settle grievances relating to land rates.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.
