Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your top concern regarding pollution in Delhi? Landfill waste Air quality Water quality (Yamuna) Dust pollution 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Focus on pollution and waste management

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: RBI rate hike impact: Bond yields may hold near 7.25% after policy shift
Article Text:
Bond yields may hold near 7.25%

Government bond yields may remain under pressure in early trade on Thursday after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) raised interest rates for the first time in nearly four years and changed its policy stance, signalling that more rate hikes could follow.The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond yield is expected to trade between 7.21% and 7.25%, a trader with a primary dealership said. The yield closed at 7.2410% on Wednesday. Bond yields rise when bond prices fall."Unless there is a fresh open market sale announcement, the 10-year benchmark should hold around 7.25% level," the trader told Reuters.The RBI raised its key interest rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%, from 5.25%, and changed its stance to "calibrated tightening" from "neutral".The central bank also raised its inflation forecast by 20 basis points to 5.2%. Its forecast for core inflation, which does not include volatile food and fuel prices, was raised to 4.4% from 4.3%.RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said the change in stance meant a "milder form of tightening" and that future decisions would depend more on incoming data rather than being decided in advance."The RBI is normalising rates to keep real rates positive rather than materially tightening financial conditions, and with close to 100 bps of hikes already priced in, most of the adjustment in yields is behind us," said Anurag Mittal, president and head of fixed income at UTI AMC.The RBI did not announce any new steps to reduce surplus liquidity in the banking system, even though the market had expected such measures. The decision was seen as slightly positive for bonds.In September, the RBI sold bonds worth 1 trillion rupees ($10.35 billion), its biggest bond sale in at least a decade.India's overnight indexed swap rates are expected to remain in a narrow range, with some consolidation around current levels after the RBI's policy decision.The one-year OIS rate ended at 6.25%, while the two-year rate closed at 6.4525%. The five-year OIS rate settled higher at 6.7225%.
Article Summary: The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond yield is expected to trade between 7.21% and 7.25% on Thursday. The yield closed at 7.2410% on Wednesday. The RBI raised its key interest rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%, from 5.25%.

Article Title: US-based daughter files case against parents seeking share in properties; Karnataka HC rejects her ‘ancestral’ claim, saying they were father's separate assets, not coparcenary property
Article Text:
Her legal argument relied significantly on Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act as amended with effect from September 9, 2005. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did the High Court rule against the daughter?

Significance of ruling

Your father has several properties in his and decides to sell one of them. Do you as a daughter have a claim on the property? In one such case, a daughter who sought a share in properties held by her father has lost her legal battle after the Karnataka High Court held that she failed to prove that the properties were ancestral or coparcenary properties in which she had acquired a right by birth.The case involved a dispute over whether properties that had come to the woman’s father from her grandfather retained the character of ancestral property, giving her a right to seek partition under the Hindu Succession Act.The woman, based in the US, has been living abroad since her marriage in 1979. She filed a suit seeking partition of family properties and an equal share in them after her father sold one property. The daughter sued her parents and sister for partition of four family properties. Her case was that the properties formed part of the Hindu joint family estate and that she was entitled to a share as a coparcener.Also Read | 83-year-old woman got Rs 12.28 lakh after son’s death, but sought Rs 15,000 maintenance from college-going granddaughter and a share of family pension from son’s widow; Kerala HC rejects both claims She also sought rights in movable and immovable assets, including family jewellery, bank deposits, share investments and debentures, which she alleged were joint family properties.The suit covered four schedule properties.The woman claimed that Schedule A was ancestral property which had fallen to her father's share. She further claimed that income generated through quarrying on that property had been used to acquire Schedule B. She also claimed that her father had inherited Schedules C and D and that the income from the family properties had contributed to the family's other assets.Her legal argument relied significantly on Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act as amended with effect from September 9, 2005. The amended provision recognises a daughter as a coparcener by birth in a Mitakshara joint Hindu family, with the same rights as a son in coparcenary property.The trial court rejected the daughter’s claim and dismissed the suit. She then approached the High Court where she lost again.The Karnataka High Court considered whether Schedules A, C and D were the self-acquired properties of the woman’s father or whether he had inherited them from his ancestors in a manner that made them joint Hindu family properties.Also Read | Man enters JDA for land, gets 6 flats from builder and transfers 5 to wife, but gets tax notice; ITAT Delhi deletes Rs 4.14 crore additions after finding no stock-in-trade conversion or sale The evidence of the daughter’s own witness became important.Her paternal uncle said Schedule A had been purchased by his father. He also admitted that the portion forming Schedule A had come to the woman’s father's share and that it was absolute property.His evidence regarding Schedule C was similar. He stated that it had also been purchased by his father and that, in the partition, Schedule C came to the woman’s father's share. He agreed that Schedule C was the father's absolute property.The High Court also found that Schedule D was the self-acquired property of the woman’s grandfather and that it came to her father's share as a result of partition.“The said witness clearly admits that the property fell to the share of defendant No.1 under the said partition/ family arrangement is his self-acquired property,” the court said.“The admissions given by PW.2 clearly indicate that the properties partitioned were the self-acquired properties of the grandfather. In such an eventuality, there cannot be any adverse opinion against the defendants for their failure to lead evidence, when the plaintiff, herself, has failed to discharge the initial burden casted upon her,” the court said.The court therefore concluded that Schedules A, C and D were not ancestral or coparcenary properties. They had become the individual and separate properties of the woman's father."These properties are neither the joint Hindu family properties nor coparcenery properties. These properties became individual/separate properties of defendant No.1,” the court said.The High Court then examined the significance of Section 6 of the Hindu Succession Act.It noted that the 2005 amendment made a daughter a coparcener by birth in a Mitakshara joint Hindu family and gave her the same rights as a son in coparcenary property. But the court stressed that the right arises in coparcenary property, not in every property owned by a parent."Thus if a property is joint Hindu family property, then only a coparcener shall acquire the right by birth and not otherwise,” it said.The High Court specifically said that if the properties in Schedules A, C and D were the grandfather's self-acquired properties, he had the right to dispose of them. Once they came to his children through the partition, they became the separate properties of those children rather than retaining a coparcenary character.The court also considered Schedule B. The Karnataka High Court's analysis stated that, even according to the woman’s case, Schedule B had been purchased from income generated from Schedule A and treated it as the father's self-acquired property. The High Court ultimately found that the woman had failed to establish that the properties claimed by her were coparcenary properties.The court said, “There was no unity of ownership and possession between all members of the family. The plaintiff was never in possession of the property, which became the self-acquired properties of her father. In the absence of unity of possession of the plaintiff along with other family members i.e. parents and defendant No.3/sister. The plaintiff did not acquire an interest by birth in the properties, which are the individual/separate properties of her father. ”“It is well settled that Mitakshara father has absolute right of disposition over his self-acquired property, to which no exception can be taken by male/female descendants,” it added.Explaining the judgement, Gaurav Dasgupta, Partner, Khaitan & Co said, “The Court drew the line clearly. What the grandfather bought with his own money was his self-acquired property, and he was free to deal with it as he wished. When he handed it to his children through a family partition, it became each child's separate property. It did not become joint family property in which grandchildren acquire rights at birth. ”“The Court added that the result is the same whether the children received it through a partition or by ordinary inheritance. A daughter's right as a coparcener applies only where the property actually has a coparcenary character, and she must prove that character first,” he tells TOI.Also Read | Woman declared Rs 67.4 lakh ancestral jewellery in her ITR which led to additions by tax department; ITAT Mumbai deleted it on basis of old records, but rejected her Rs 12 lakh HUF brokerage claim Gaurav Dasgupta says daughter's right by birth covers ancestral property, not her father's own property or even a property which has been gifted to her father or her father had acquired by way of a partition/settlement from his own father.“Only when a person inherits a property from any one of his three immediate paternal ancestors, his sons, grandsons and great grandsons, acquire an interest in it by birth or under Section 6 of the Hindus Succession act, after amendment w.e.f. 09.09.2005,” he tells TOI.According to Dasgupta, this judgment is a timely reminder that the landmark 2005 reform giving daughters equal coparcenary rights is powerful, but it is not a blank cheque.“Many people now assume that a daughter can claim a share in anything her father owns. That is not the law, and this ruling explains why. However, post the death of the father, in case of intestate succession, she will be treated equally like her siblings at the time of determination of succession,” he adds.According to Dasgupta, what this settles is the distinction families most often get wrong: 'property from my grandfather' is not automatically 'ancestral property'. What it leaves open is what happens after the father dies. His separate property then passes under the ordinary succession rules, unless he has made a will or a gift. That is a separate claim, and this partition suit did not decide it, he says.He advises that before suing for partition, it’s important to trace how each property was first acquired and collect the documents, such as old partition deeds and purchase records.
Article Summary: The case involved a dispute over whether properties that had come to the woman’s father from her grandfather retained the character of ancestral property. The woman, based in the US, has been living abroad since her marriage in 1979. She filed a suit seeking partition of family properties and an equal share in them.

Article Title: Indian company inked agreement with Powerus 3 months before US firm signed pact with Pakistan
Article Text:
Guardian-1 counter-drone interceptor

NEW DELHI: Navi Mumbai-based Paras Defence Space and Technology, which recently signed a licencing agreement to produce and sell Guardian-1 counter-drone interceptor with Trump-linked firm Powerus Corporation — the same US company that has also entered into a defence deal with Pakistan military, on Wednesday said that its “objective from the outset has been to contribute to strengthening India’s defence preparedness”.Paras Defence had signed the agreement on June 30 with Tandem Defence, a wholly owned subsidiary of Powerus Corporation, that granted it exclusive intellectual property licence to produce and sell the Guardian-1 high-speed battery-powered interceptor in India. But the pact was inked three months before Powerus representatives met the Pakistan military leadership in Rawalpindi, secured a limited procurement order for the counter-drone interceptor and signed an MoU with Pakistan army last Sept.Responding to a TOI query, Paras Defence, in a statement, said, “We were among the earliest to identify the potential of this technology (Guardian-1 counter-drone interceptor) and initiate discussions to bring the capability to India. Our objective from the outset has been to facilitate technology transfer, build indigenous capability and contribute to strengthening India’s defence preparedness. In line with this objective, Powerus’ role under the partnership is primarily focused on technology transfer, while the larger objective is to build indigenous manufacturing and capability in India.The Maharashtra-based company further said, “Our focus remains on developing and strengthening India-centric defence capabilities, with the technology and know-how being adapted to meet the specific requirements of the Indian defence ecosystem.”Powerus has reported financial ties to Donald Trump Jr and Eric Trump, prompting regional security discussions in India regarding shared military hardware suppliers and the transfer of unmanned systems across rival countries.Since its inception in 2009, Paras Defence has been manufacturing advanced light machine guns like MK-46 and MK-48 LMGs, laser weapon systems, and weaponised tactical drones.It has also partnered with DRDO to develop laser source modules and signed a technology transfer agreement to indigenously manufacture driver night sight systems, developed by DRDO, for Indian Army’s T-90 main battle tanks.
Article Summary: Navi Mumbai-based Paras Defence Space and Technology recently signed a licencing agreement to produce and sell Guardian-1 counter-drone interceptor. Paras Defence said its “objective from the outset has been to contribute to strengthening India’s defence preparedness”

Article Title: Oil remains beyond $100 per barrel as Middle East supply concerns persist
Article Text:
Crude oil prices continue to rally

Oil prices inched higher on Thursday as concerns over supply from the Middle East intensified amid a rise in attacks on vessels in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz.Brent crude was trading at $101.50 a barrel, up $1.32 or 1.32%, while WTI crude stood at $89.28, gaining $1 or 1.13%.The latest gains come despite a fall in prices in the previous session, when the International Energy Agency agreed to speed up the release of oil stocks and give priority to diesel supplies. The plan, launched in March, is aimed at dealing with record fuel prices and supply disruptions linked to the Iran war.Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz has become a growing concern as the US-Israeli conflict with Iran enters its eighth month. Before the war, the route handled shipments equivalent to about 20% of global oil and fuel supplies.The pressure on shipping has increased even as Gulf producers raise exports. Tanker attacks through the Strait reached their highest level last week for any week since the Iran war began, leaving crude shipments facing higher costs and greater risks for cargoes and crew.A tanker north of Qatar was struck by multiple projectiles in the latest attack, causing casualties, the United Kingdom maritime trade operations agency said on Wednesday.Supply concerns were accompanied by signs of tighter US inventories. According to Reuters, American crude stocks fell by 3.2 million barrels in the week ended October 2 to 424.1 million barrels, according to the Energy Information Administration. The decline was larger than the 1.7 million-barrel fall analysts had expected in a Reuters poll.Diesel and jet fuel inventories also declined, with distillate fuel stocks falling by 42,000 barrels to 105.14 million barrels. Those inventories remained below their levels for this period of the year over the past five years.Oil markets have remained unsettled for more than seven months since the Middle East conflict began. Even with the latest increase, prices are still below the $126 a barrel level reached earlier in the crisis.
Article Summary: Brent crude was trading at $101.50 a barrel, up $1.32 or 1.32%. WTI crude stood at $89.28, gaining $1 or1.13%. The latest gains come despite a fall in prices in the previous session.

Article Title: Rupee rises 10 paise against US dollar: What is supporting the currency?
Article Text:
Rupee rises 10 paise against US dollar

Rupee began Thursday on a positive note, recovering 10 paise to trade at 96.65 against the US dollar in early deals. The recovery comes amid likely intervention by the Reserve Bank of India , which may have helped the currency hold ground despite continued pressure from global and domestic factors.The currency had opened at 96.71 at the interbank foreign exchange market before moving up to 96.65. Earlier on Wednesday, it ended at 96.75 against the dollar.Despite the early recovery, forex traders said the rupee remained under pressure from a combination of a stronger US dollar, elevated crude oil prices and sustained foreign fund outflows. The DXY was trading near multi-month highs, while Brent crude remained around the $102-a-barrel mark.The decline in India's forex reserves has added to the pressure on investor sentiment. Reserves have fallen by $50 billion in three weeks from the September peak of $786 billion."Strong corporate importer demand for dollars together with safe-haven capital shifts overpowered the RBI's hawkish policy stance, driving USD/INR higher through the afternoon until routine state-run bank interventions helped stem further losses," said Anil Kumar Bhansali head of treasury and executive director Finrex Treasury Advisors LLP.Market participants are now looking towards the RBI for action against speculation in the USD/INR pair. Forex traders said the RBI Governor has assured that the central bank would help the rupee find its true value, with the currency presently considered undervalued.The dollar index was at 102.25, gaining 0.01% against a basket of six currencies.Oil prices, meanwhile, remained elevated. Brent crude futures climbed 2.17% to $102.37 per barrel as concerns over disruptions to supplies through the Strait of Hormuz weighed on the market."The main reason for the rebound in crude oil prices is persistent concern over Middle East supply and shipping disruptions, particularly with attacks on tankers in the Gulf and around the Strait of Hormuz intensifying," Bhansali said.The pressure on the currency came alongside weakness in domestic equities. BSE Sensex was down 264.97 points at 72,408.15 in early trade, while NSE Nifty50 declined 87.50 points to 22,507.65.Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) were net sellers in Indian equities on Wednesday, offloading shares worth Rs 6,121.37 crore, according to exchange data.
Article Summary: Rupee recovers 10 paise to trade at 96.65 against US dollar in early deals. Recovery comes amid likely intervention by the Reserve Bank of India. Rupee under pressure from a stronger US dollar, elevated crude oil prices and sustained foreign fund outflows.

Article Title: US mortgage rates jump to 7.49%, hit highest level in nearly 3 years
Article Text:
US mortgage rate climbs to three year high

US mortgage rates have soared to their highest level in nearly three years, with the sharp rise in borrowing costs adding to pressure on the housing market as Americans head towards November 3 elections.The average rate for a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rose 19 basis points to 7.49% in the week ended October 2, the Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA) said, as cited by Reuters. This spike pushed rates to the highest level since November 2023, hitting demand for home loans.Mortgage applications dropped 4.2% last week from the previous week, while refinancing applications fell sharply. Overall application volumes are now at their lowest since February 2025 and have declined nearly 50% since January."Very few homeowners have an incentive to refinance at these rates, and the jump in borrowing costs has caused many potential borrowers to step back from the purchase market," Joel Kan, the MBA’s deputy chief economist told Reuters.Mortgage rates have closely followed movements in the yield on 10-year US treasury notes. Earlier this week, the yield topped 5.3%, reaching a 24-year high, with concerns over inflationary pressures from soaring oil prices and data showing stronger US economic growth driving the rise.Home borrowing rates are up about 1.4 percentage points since joint US-Israeli strikes against Iran began in late February, tracking a similar increase in the 10-year treasury yield.The increase comes at a politically sensitive time, with the US mid-term elections just four weeks away. The cost of living was the top issue among Americans in deciding how they would vote, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday. At the same time, US President Donald Trump's approval rating stood at a record low of 32%.Inflation has also risen, reaching 3.4% in August on a measure targeted by the Federal Reserve at 2%.Fed policymakers have signalled that they expect another interest-rate increase by the end of the year following the rate hike in September. Markets are currently betting that policymakers will not raise rates at the next meeting at the end of October.The latest increase in mortgage rates comes as affordability remains under pressure for buyers, while the decline in loan applications points to weaker activity in the mortgage market.
Article Summary: US mortgage rates have soared to their highest level in nearly three years. The average rate for a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rose 19 basis points to 7.49%. This spike pushed rates to the highest level since November 2023, hitting demand for home loans.

Article Title: Russia eyes return to Europe's gas market despite sanctions, Ukraine war: Report
Article Text:
Russia aims to reach Europe’s gas market through Nord Stream pipeline (Representational image)

Nord Stream back on the table

Restarting gas flows won't be easy

Germany split over Russian gas

Who owns Nord Stream?

Lukoil assets also in focus

Russia may be looking to turn the gas taps to Europe back on, with talks under way over bringing a US investor into the Nord Stream pipelines that once carried Russian gas to Germany.According to five people familiar with the matter, the discussions involve US Special Envoy Jared Kushner and Kirill Dmitriev, a close adviser to Russian President Vladimir Putin.Kushner, who has been trying to broker a truce between Russia and Ukraine, sees business deals as central to restoring peace. A potential Nord Stream deal could allow US investors to profit from energy flows to Europe once the war ends.Kushner and Dmitriev have met in Moscow and New York in recent weeks. Two sources told Reuters that Nord Stream remains on the agenda, although not much details are available about the discussions.Dmitriev, who has been pushing for Russian gas sales to Germany to resume, met representatives of the US energy and treasury departments last month, to discuss potential US-Russia energy initiatives.A White House official said that any deals would have to be negotiated with the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) and Treasury and must benefit US taxpayers and companies."Any deals will have to be negotiated by Russia with DFC (US International Development Finance Corporation) and Treasury and must benefit United States taxpayers and companies," the official said.The official also said there had been "no Nord Stream discussions recently".A return of Russian gas to Germany still faces several hurdles. The Nord Stream pipelines are sanctioned by the US and the EU, making any restart illegal.A US official said a deal was unlikely in the medium term because of the obstacles involved. US President Donald Trump could waive or soften US sanctions, but that would become harder if Democrats win control of Congress in next month's midterm elections.Germany and other European countries are also expected to oppose reopening Nord Stream. They are spending billions of euros rebuilding their military to defend themselves from Russia.A spokeswoman for Germany's economy and energy ministry said Nord Stream and Russian gas were sanctioned in Europe and that Germany had found alternatives. She said reopening the pipelines would require government approval and was not desired.Before Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Germany bought more than half of its gas from Russia through the two Nord Stream pipelines. They were mothballed after Moscow throttled supplies to Europe and were blown up in a series of underwater explosions in September 2022.The idea of bringing Russian gas back to Germany has also divided opinion within the country.Germany's coalition government is opposed to restarting the pipeline, while Alternative for Germany (AfD), the country's most popular political party, wants to reopen it. Dmitriev is due to meet AfD leadership early next year to discuss selling Russian gas again.Poland is also watching the discussions but remains firmly opposed to reopening the pipeline, according to one person familiar with the government's thinking. Poland and the Baltic states are particularly vulnerable to Russia and reject energy ties.The talks are taking place against a backdrop of deep European mistrust of Russia's motives. Earlier this year, the heads of five European spy agencies told Reuters that Russia did not want to end the war quickly and was using US talks to push for business deals instead.Relations between Russia and Germany, which is among the biggest providers of military support to Ukraine, have hit a low ebb. Officials in Berlin have accused Russia of mounting a systematic campaign of hybrid attacks.Some German lawmakers say business deals would bolster Moscow as it pursues war with Ukraine."This threatens to be a dirty deal that will cost Europe dearly," said Michael Kellner, a lawmaker who was in charge of German energy policy in the aftermath of the Ukraine invasion."Americans and Russians will share the profits," he said.Ownership could be another hurdle for any US investment in Nord Stream.Russian state energy giant Gazprom owns 51% of the company. Another 31% is split between two German entities, while the remaining stake is held by a French and a Dutch firm.The two German shareholders want to retain their stakes to maintain German influence if Gazprom sells its share, another person familiar with the matter said.Days after the Moscow meetings, Kushner said in Kyiv that he had spoken to European counterparts about how the war had pushed up energy prices. He advocated "prosperity agreements" to encourage peace and give "leaders ... something to look forward to".Kushner and Dmitriev have also discussed the possible sale of businesses owned by Russian energy company Lukoil, including oil refineries and petrol stations in Europe and elsewhere, two people familiar with the matter said.Under the proposal, a consortium involving the DFC and investors from Qatar and the United Arab Emirates would buy the assets, while US authorities would lift sanctions, the people said."On Lukoil, Steve (Witkoff) and Jared (Kushner) worked with DFC to negotiate a substantial upfront payment and profits interest for the United States," a White House official said.
Article Summary: Talks under way over bringing a US investor into the Nord Stream pipelines that once carried Russian gas to Germany. US Special Envoy Jared Kushner sees business deals as central to restoring peace. A potential Nord Stream deal could allow US investors to profit from energy flows to Europe.

Article Title: Bombay HC to X: Remove video against Serum Institute, Adar Poonawalla
Article Text:
Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to take down a recent video uploaded by Yohan Tengra.





MUMBAI: Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to remove a video against Serum Institute of India Pvt Ltd and its CEO Adar Poonawalla that was uploaded by a social media influencer Yohan Tengra immediately after its June 5, 2023 order.Justice Gauri Godse of HC on Tuesday passed the order on SII and Poonawalla’s interim application in the pending defamation suit regarding content posted against the company and its COVID-19 vaccine. She also issued show-cause notices to Tengra, his organisation Anarchy for Freedom India, Ambar Koiri and TV 10 L.I.V.E, an online news portal, as to why action should not be taken for defying HC’s order. The notices are returnable on Oct 27.The application said Tengra and four defendants were restrained by the June 5, 2023 order from publishing or circulating defamatory videos and content. The same night Tengra uploaded a fresh video. On June 9, 2023, the plaintiffs issued a takedown notice to Google and X. Google complied but X refused, stating HC’s order was not issued against it.Advocate Karl Tamboly, for SII and Poonawalla, said videos uploaded were held to be unlawful by the June 5, 2023 order.Hence, videos and content of a like nature are also directed to be removed. He said in the absence of Tengra complying with HC’s direction, X is obligated to remove the objectionable content. Advocate Mayur Khandeparkar, for X, said the plaintiffs must initiate contempt proceedings against the defendants instead of waging a proxy battle with an intermediary.Justice Godse said it is undisputed that the objectionable content is still available with X. Tengra uploaded the fresh video not only in blatant defiance of HC’s injunction order “but he also states that he will not comply with the directions of the court and that he would not stop calling plaintiff no. 2 (Poonawalla) ‘a mass murderer’.”The judge noted there were no directions to X to remove the objectionable content and, thus, it cannot be held liable for the objectionable content not removed by the five defendants or for the new content uploaded by Tengra. Citing a Supreme Court judgment, she said even if an intermediary is exempt from liability for third-party information, necessary directions can be issued to remove the unlawful or prohibited content.Considering the “subsequent circumstance” of Tengra uploading the fresh video, Justice Godse said sufficient grounds are made out to direct X to “remove, delete or disable access” to the fresh video uploaded by Tengra.
Article Summary: Bombay High Court has directed X Corp to remove a video against Serum Institute of India Pvt Ltd and its CEO Adar Poonawalla. The video was uploaded by social media influencer Yohan Tengra immediately after its June 5, 2023 order.

Article Title: India's factory growth hits 7 month high in September, thanks to demand and hiring boost
Article Text:
Factory growth hits 7-month high, PMI rises to 55.1

India’s manufacturing activity scaled up sharply in September, as stronger demand pushed up sales and production, while companies stepped up hiring and stock-building.The seasonally adjusted HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 55.1 in September, from 52.8 in August, marking the strongest improvement in the sector’s health in seven months. A PMI reading above 50 indicates expansion, while a reading below 50 signals contraction.The recovery in factory activity was supported by both domestic and overseas demand. Stronger new orders helped drive production higher, with demand across electronics, food, pharma and textiles taking total sales growth to its highest level since February.Export orders also gained momentum during the month, with manufacturers reporting increased business from clients in Brazil, Europe, the UAE and the US."India's factory sector ended the quarter on a firmer footing. The PMI rose to 55.1 in September, up from 52.8, as stronger domestic and overseas demand lifted sales and production. Hiring resumed at its fastest pace since May, and manufacturers became more optimistic about the months ahead," Pranjul Bhandari, chief India economist at HSBC, told PTI.The improvement in demand was accompanied by a renewed increase in factory employment.After a blip in August, job growth resumed in September, with the pace of employment expansion described by panellists as solid and the strongest since May.Manufacturers also became more confident about the months ahead. Output forecasts were upgraded during September, taking overall positive sentiment to a four-month high. The outlook was supported by a healthy pipeline of new enquiries and expectations that strong demand would continue.The expectation of higher future sales also prompted companies to increase their purchases of materials and build inventories. Overall buying activity expanded at a faster pace than in August."Companies bought more materials and built up stocks to prepare for anticipated sales. Finished goods inventories recorded their second-largest increase in nearly 12 years, signalling a clear shift from leaner stock levels," Bhandari said.Finished goods inventories rose for the third consecutive month. The increase was the second-fastest in 11-and-a-half years, behind July, as manufacturers actively accumulated stocks in anticipation of stronger demand.At the same time, companies faced quicker increases in input costs and selling prices. Despite the acceleration, the rates of inflation remained mild by historical standards.The September reading came as manufacturing activity regained momentum after the slower expansion recorded in August, with the PMI rising by more than two points during the month."Holdings of finished products increased for the third month in a row and at the second-fastest pace in 11-and-a-half years (behind July)," the report said.The HSBC India Manufacturing PMI is compiled by S&P Global based on responses from purchasing managers at around 400 manufacturers.
Article Summary: HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) rose to 55.1 in September, from 52.8 in August. Stronger new orders helped drive production higher, with demand across electronics, food, pharma and textiles taking total sales growth to its highest level since February.

Article Title: Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses
Article Text:
Anthropic targets $2 trillion valuation despite huge spending and billions in losses

Revenue growth draws investor attention

Huge infrastructure spending

Losses add to valuation questions

Customer concentration remains a risk

Anthropic has put a massive price tag on the AI boom, backing it with an equally heavy spending plan.The AI giant is heading towards a potential valuation of more than $2 trillion even as it plans $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations in the coming years.The company’s IPO prospectus, seen by Reuters, also shows just how quickly its business has grown. Anthropic’s revenue reportedly rose 12-fold in 2025, giving investors a strong growth story to weigh against its continuing losses and huge infrastructure commitments.The scale of its plans has also spilled into markets, with European technology shares rising 2.4% and the US chip index gaining 1.5%.For investors, Anthropic’s rapid expansion is a key part of the valuation story.Michael Field, chief equity strategist at Morningstar, Amsterdam, said the speed of the company’s growth stood out in the prospectus."If anything, the acceleration of the business is the biggest part of this release. Growing a big business can be difficult, but the prospectus stating that revenue grew by 12 fold in 2025 is truly remarkable."Field said the proposed valuation should be considered alongside the company’s sales."Obviously a $2 trillion valuation sounds outlandish, but when you break it down to a multiple of sales, likely to be around 18-20x, it sounds much more reasonable than the recent SpaceX IPO."Anthropic’s plans also show that the AI investment cycle is continuing to require substantial spending on infrastructure.Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB Platform, London, said the planned spending was positive for companies involved in semiconductors and AI infrastructure."This is positive for the AI trade, since it is fuelled by continued elevated levels of capex spend. The fact that Anthropic is planning on spending big on capex means that the capex cycle is not over yet. This is good news for semiconductor and AI infrastructure companies. I believe that if Anthropic had signalled a lower level of spending, this could have caused a wobble in the AI trade, since it would lead to fears about the sustainability of the AI trade as we move into Q4. "The prospectus puts rapid revenue growth alongside the large infrastructure commitments needed to support it.Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club, London, said Anthropic’s expectations for AI’s economic impact appeared to have supported demand for European technology stocks."It's the vision and the projections to the extent to which Anthropic believes AI will be a game changer for economies around the world that seem to have lifted demand for European tech stocks."She also raised concerns over the company’s spending while it remains loss-making."There still will be niggles of concern among some about the huge sums that are projected to be spent even though it is making a loss. But that hasn't caused a flutter of general fear because, overall, there still seems to be a pretty hefty appetite for AI focused investments."Anthropic’s losses remain another factor in the debate around its proposed valuation.Field said the losses were a concern when considered against the company’s current revenue, growth rate and size. However, he said investors had already absorbed much of the spending story."The losses certainly are a concern. Particularly given the growth rate and the size relative to current revenues. It's unlikely to deter investors, however, with the spend story having been digested for some time now."He said the scale of planned investment also reflected management’s confidence in future demand."The key takeaway for investors is the confidence in the business and the AI strategy. Yes spend is high and growing, but management obviously feel the growth rate inherent in demand is sufficiently attractive to keep spending, hence why they are coming to market and demanding a top-dollar valuation."Anthropic’s revenue growth is another area attracting attention, particularly because a significant share reportedly comes from a small number of customers.Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell, London, said the company’s revenue growth had become the main focus despite its spending plans. "Massive spending would normally have investors running for the hills, but what's capturing the market's attention is Anthropic's stellar revenue growth, up 12-fold in 2025. Admittedly, AI is moving at such a rapid pace that last year’s sales achievements relate to technology that is already outdated. "Anthropic’s IPO plans therefore bring together rapid revenue growth, continuing losses and a huge infrastructure commitment. The company is seeking a valuation of more than $2 trillion while planning $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations.
Article Summary: Anthropic is heading towards a potential valuation of more than $2 trillion. It plans $518 billion in cloud computing and infrastructure obligations in the coming years. Anthropic’s revenue reportedly rose 12-fold in 2025, giving investors a strong growth story to weigh against its continuing losses.

Article Title: RBI rate hikes ahead? BofA sees 100 bps repo rate increase through H1 2027
Article Text:
BofA sees 100 bps repo rate increase through H1 2027

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) could raise interest rates by 100 basis points through the first half of 2027, according to Bank of America (BofA) Securities. The brokerage has also moved up its estimate for the first rate hike, now expecting the hike in October instead of December.BofA expects the RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points at its October 7 monetary policy meeting, and then another 75 basis points of hikes, taking the projected terminal rate to 6.25 per cent.The new forecast is twice the size of BofA's earlier 50 basis point estimate.“Our bigger forecast shift is arguably the quantum of hikes, as we are raising our total quantum of hikes from 50bp earlier, to 100bp now,” BofA said.BofA expects the RBI to raise rates by 50 basis points in the fourth quarter of 2026 and another 50 basis points in the first half of 2027. It also expects the central bank to change its monetary policy stance in December.“The RBI will switch the stance in December to one of calibrated tightening”, the report said.So, what has changed in BofA's view? The brokerage said the domestic economy remains resilient, giving the RBI less reason to wait before raising rates.At the same time, inflation risks are becoming broader.Oil prices remained around $100-110 per barrel for most of September, BofA said. It also pointed to rising risks of fuel price increases and food-related supply pressures.Strong economic growth is another factor behind the revised outlook. BofA said the strength of the economy is reducing the need for the RBI to keep monetary conditions accommodative.Non-food credit growth stood at 17.8 per cent year-on-year in September, while investment demand is expected to remain healthy in the second quarter of FY27.Inflation pressures are also spreading, according to the report. BofA said food inflation is becoming more broad-based, while wholesale inflation is increasingly spreading to other sectors. Tradables inflation rose to 5.9 per cent in August 2026.The brokerage has also laid out a scenario in which the RBI could go beyond the 100-basis-point increase it currently expects. If real GDP growth stays around 7 per cent and headline inflation remains close to 5.5 per cent, BofA said the central bank could raise rates by more than 100 basis points.In that case, front-end rates could rise above 6.5 per cent, the brokerage said.But a sharp slowdown in growth could change the rate outlook. BofA said the RBI could deliver fewer hikes or no hike if growth falls below 7 per cent and moves towards 6 per cent on a forward-looking basis.
Article Summary: Bank of America Securities sees 100 bps repo rate increase through H1 2027. BofA expects the RBI to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points at its October 7 monetary policy meeting, and then another 75 basis points of hikes, taking the projected terminal rate to 6.25 per cent.
